I read that saffron needs loamy soil. I want to grow it in doors. What is loamy soil and how do I make it from what I see in Lowes?

[edit]

Oops, I meant loamy.

Best way to describe it is this; loamy should be nice and rich, dark brown or black. You should be able to squish a handful and then have it somewhat hold together, but then crumble when you rub your thumb over it.

Lowes... for saffron... not a great idea.

Go to a local hydroponics store, they'll have way better quality materials. You need living soil for saffron, so I suggest taking a bunch from your current outdoor garden and mixing in 1/4 volume perlite, add in generous mychorizhal fungi, and possibly a small amount of lime. Let sit for 2 weeks and go ahead and use it!

You're attempting to grow one of the most expensive items on the planet per volume. Definitely have patience. Would love photos of your process!

Loamy is not too sandy, not too clay-like. Clay soil, if you take a clump of it in your hand, will form a clump kind of like play-doh and if you try to crumble it, it will crumble in larger pieces. Sandy soil is the opposite of clay - hard to form a clump. Loamy soil will clump fairly well but also crumble a little finer than clay. Ugh, I should not drink and voat.

Do you have any access to a yard? You could just use that soil and amend it with proper fertilizer. I'm more familiar with dealing with clay soil, so I don't have much to offer if you have sandy soil. I think I used a 5/10/10 compost to amend my clay soil, about half compost half clay worked for my beds.

Loam is that which is not clay or sand.

Usually having significant amounts of organic (carbon-based) matter within it. Usually drains well. High nutrient/mineral content.
